why: The criterion holds. I checked every name and claim in the issue against the repository. bin/greet.js does pick the first argument that doesn't start with '--' and ignores flags, so `--shout Ada` really prints `Hello, Ada!`. src/greet.js exports `greeting(name)` returning `Hello, ${name}!`. docs/index.md documents only `node bin/greet.js <name>`. pages.yml uploads `docs` on pushes to main, and the README gives https://o.github.io/greet-cli/ as the docs URL. `npm test` exists as `node --test`. The usage message `usage: greet <name>` and exit code 2 match the code. test/ exists. The claim that README "only links to the docs site" is accurate. Writing `greet --shout <name>` in the outcome follows the request's wording, and every check uses `node bin/greet.js`. No file, script or function is invented, and the problem statement describes the code as it is.
